claims.sourceText: Dean Rickles, 'The Chapel Hill Conference in Context'
claims.text: Trimble described the body he proposed as an 'industrial version of the Institute for Advanced Study'. The Glenn L. Martin Company's institute was 'industry-sponsored, and not ensconced in a university', while the Institute of Field Physics was deliberately placed inside the University of North Carolina 'so as to avoid the conflict that physicists felt working in an industrial setting.'

claims.sourceText: Trimble to Bryce DeWitt, 10 June 1955, quoted by Dean Rickles in the Edition Open Sources edition of the 1957 Chapel Hill conference report
claims.text: In a letter to Bryce DeWitt dated 10 June 1955, Trimble wrote: 'It occurred to us some time ago that our industry was vitally concerned with gravity. As time goes on we become more and more concerned because we feel certain that sooner or later man will invade space and we see it as our job to do everything possible to speed this event. At least one category of the things one must study, when he desires to bring space flight to reality, is the laws of nature surrounding the force of gravity.'

claims.sourceText: Dean Rickles, 'The Chapel Hill Conference in Context', in the Edition Open Sources edition of the 1957 conference report
